question.problem: The mass density function $\lambda ,$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ of a thin rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 2$ is given by $\lambda (x)=4{x}^{3}-3,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?
question.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b,$ if $\lambda (x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by  

$$
m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=4{x}^{3}-3,\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

  

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4{x}^{3}-3\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{x}^{4}-3x]_{1}^{2} \\  & =(16-6)-(1-3) \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $12\,\text{kg}.$
